prompt.context: Our client is a private equity firm interested in Plastic World, a plastic packaging manufacturer. Plastic World's owners are requesting $25m. The offer is final.
prompt.question: Should our client buy the company for $25m?

clarifying_info.a: Plastic packaging for beverages, cosmetics, household and automotive chemicals. Products are top quality; they have 350 sets of molds with different materials, finish, and colors, and they are always innovating.

clarifying_info.q: Has the product mix changed recently?
clarifying_info.a: No, overall product mix has not changed in recent years.

clarifying_info.q: How is the sales force structured?
clarifying_info.a: The sales force is considered 'the best in breed'; they hold market share and are compensated based on market share.
Two years ago they invested further in equipment for product innovation.

clarifying_info.q: What are Plastic World's customers like?
clarifying_info.a: Plastic World's customers exhibit strong loyalty. They are experiencing increasing pressures in their industries to innovate plastic packaging.

exhibits.title: Profit & Loss Statement
exhibits.shows: Three-year P&L with rows for Sales ($), Volume (units), COGS ($), SG&A ($), Depreciation ($), and EBIT ($) for 2016, 2017, and 2018.

exhibits.title: Competitor Profit Margins
exhibits.shows: Bar chart of profit margins (%) for Plastic World and six competitors (A through F). The x-axis shows profit margin from approximately -10% to +15%.

exhibits.title: Valuation by Profit Margin
exhibits.shows: Scatter/line chart showing Company Valuation ($m) on the y-axis (0 to 50) versus Profit Margin (%) on the x-axis (-10 to 15). Shows the relationship between improving profit margin and company valuation.

framework: Understand current financial performance: analyze P&L trends in revenue, volume, costs, and EBIT
Diagnose root cause of profitability decline: pricing vs. cost structure vs. sales incentives
Benchmark against competitors: assess whether the problem is industry-wide or company-specific
Assess feasibility of profit margin improvement and path to profitability
Value the business under improved scenarios using the valuation curve
Provide a buy/no-buy recommendation with implementation steps

questions.prompt: Examine the P&L (Exhibit A). What observations can you make, and what might explain the trends?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify: (1) Revenue is declining despite volume growing — implies average price per unit is falling. (2) EBIT has moved from +$1.45m in 2016 to -$1.18m in 2018 — the company is now loss-making. (3) COGS and SG&A have grown modestly, but the large jump in depreciation in 2017 (from $2.25m to $3.45m) reflects the equipment investment. (4) Because product mix is unchanged and volume is up, the revenue drop must be price-driven. (5) The interviewer should independently surface — or be guided to — the sales force compensation structure: sales reps are paid on market share, incentivizing them to lower prices to win volume. This explains the paradox of growing volume with falling revenue. Candidate should also note product quality and customer loyalty mean price cuts are not necessary to retain customers.

questions.prompt: Request and interpret competitor profit margin data (Exhibit B). What does this tell you about Plastic World's situation?
questions.guidance: The key insight is that all competitors are profitable (ranging roughly 2% to 13%), while Plastic World is at approximately -6%. This confirms the profitability problem is company-specific, not an industry-wide downturn. A strong candidate will push to establish a realistic target margin for Plastic World — the industry average appears to be roughly 6-10%. Candidate should connect this back to the sales force incentive diagnosis and note that fixing the incentive structure is an easy, high-impact lever.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit C (Valuation by Profit Margin), assess whether the $25m purchase price is justified and what upside exists.
questions.guidance: The chart shows that a 0% profit margin corresponds to a valuation of approximately $25m — meaning Plastic World at breakeven is worth exactly what the sellers are asking. If profit margin reaches the industry average (roughly 6-10%), the valuation rises to approximately $40m. A strong candidate concludes: (1) The $25m price is justified only if the PE firm can improve profitability above zero. (2) The easy fix — changing sales force compensation from market-share-based to earnings-based — is sufficient to get there. (3) Additional upside comes from rationalizing the 350-mold product line (cut costs while preserving innovation for customers who face packaging innovation pressure). (4) The deal creates value if these changes are implemented; at current -6% margin the company is being purchased at roughly fair value or slight premium relative to its current state.

math.setup: Read valuation at key margin points from Exhibit C
steps: At -6% margin (current): valuation ≈ below $25m (being sold near or slightly above intrinsic value)
math.answer: Buying at $25m and reaching industry-average margins implies ~$15m value creation (from $25m to $40m)

brainstorming.prompt: What changes should the PE firm implement after acquiring Plastic World to improve profitability?

categories.name: Sales force incentives
ideas: Change compensation from market-share-based to earnings/profit-based
Align bonuses with EBIT or gross margin targets instead of volume

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Raise prices to reflect product quality and customer loyalty
Implement value-based pricing given customers' need for innovation
Reduce or eliminate discretionary discounting by sales reps

categories.name: Product line rationalization
ideas: Eliminate underperforming or low-margin molds from the 350-mold set
Prioritize molds aligned with customer innovation needs
Reduce complexity in materials, finishes, and colors where there is no customer demand

categories.name: Cost management
ideas: Review SG&A for savings now that pricing is corrected
Assess depreciation load and capital allocation going forward
Benchmark COGS against industry to find manufacturing efficiencies

categories.name: Industry best practices
ideas: Benchmark against profitable competitors on operations and pricing
Explore whether any competitors have been acquired or partnerships are available

recommendation: Our client should accept the $25m offer and acquire Plastic World

The acquisition is attractive because the profitability problem is company-specific and fixable: the core issue is a misaligned sales force compensation structure that incentivizes price-cutting despite high product quality and loyal customers
If profit margin is raised to the industry average through incentive realignment and product line simplification, the company would be worth approximately $40m — implying ~$15m in value creation
risks: If the sales force resists compensation changes, the pricing problem may persist
Simplifying the product line risks losing customers who value the breadth of innovation options
Competitors could gain share during a transition period
next_steps: Immediately redesign sales force compensation to reward earnings rather than market share
Conduct a SKU/mold rationalization analysis to identify which of the 350 molds to retain vs. retire
Benchmark operations against industry best practices to identify additional margin improvement
Monitor customer retention closely during the transition
